EGPC is also the dominant supplier, with 16.3bn of purchases in the same half. That two-sided relationship is the real governance fact, and it is disclosed. Audited consolidated FS, transition period 1-Jul-2025 to 31-Dec-2025, Crowe unqualified, 18-Feb-2026

line_vol_growth.source: Volume growth by AUDITED product line. The RANKING is taken from the line-level value growth actually printed between the two disclosed halves — wax +21.3%, fuel oil +29.1%, LPG +18.7%, while gas oil (-1.9%) and naphtha (-7.3%) FELL — rather than from a view about the business. Levels are struck well below those half-on-half rates because a single half is not a trend. This is one of only two free operating parameters left and it is sensitised end to end

line_price_growth.source: Growth in the realised price per tonne, all lines, in EGP. The realisation ITSELF is disclosed — note 14-A value divided by note 14-A tonnes — so only its growth is forecast. Struck below the assumed exchange-rate path on the view that a pass-through processor recovers currency in price with a lag. The second and last free operating parameter

fixed_cost_infl.source: Cumulative-year Egyptian inflation factors applied to the pound-denominated cost legs — salaries inside cost of sales, the other line, administrative and marketing expense, and capital expenditure. Historical years as printed, easing toward the central bank's published target thereafter

payout_reported.source: Dividend payout ratio COMPUTED from the filings: cash dividends actually PAID in the audited nine months (736,577,469 in the transition half plus 602,957,265 in Q1-2026) over group profit after tax for the same nine months. Not a reported ratio and not an assumption — the two cash-flow statements divided by the two profit lines

dps.source: Dividend per share, cash actually paid in the audited nine months over shares outstanding. Annualising is left to the reader; the study uses the paid figure

e1_pe.source: Expert 1's justified price/earnings multiple. Struck below the main normalised lens deliberately: it is an independent opinion, not a re-run of the house view

proc_intensity.source: Processing intensity by product line, relative weights, used to allocate the note 15-A conversion stack (salaries, supporting materials, other, depreciation) across the eight disclosed lines. Base oils are the reference at 1.00: they pass the full lube train — vacuum distillation, solvent extraction, dewaxing, hydrofinishing. Paraffin wax carries 1.15 for the additional deoiling and sweating steps. Gas oil, naphtha and LPG are light ends drawn off the front of the process and carry 0.25/0.20/0.15. Fuel oil and heavy fuel oil are the residue, sold substantially as produced, at 0.05. THIS IS THE ONLY OPERATING INPUT IN THE MODEL THAT IS NOT READ OFF A FILING, and it exists because note 15-A discloses the cost stack for the company and not by line. It is stated here rather than hidden in a formula, and the valuation is sensitised to it

raw_pass.source: Pass-through factor on the raw-material line: 1.0 means the feedstock charge moves one-for-one with realisation and volume, so the gross SPREAD per tonne is held flat in real terms and the margin neither widens nor narrows by assumption. Setting it below 1.0 is the way to express spread widening; the study leaves it at parity and sensitises it

brent_path.source: Brent crude reference path, USD a barrel, 2026E-2030E. A flat-to-slowly-rising deck. In the previous edition this input drove NOTHING — it was registered, published in the source register and read by no line of the model. It is now the spine of both sides of the margin: every product realisation is this deck times a crack multiple solved from the disclosed product table, and the feedstock charge is this deck times a differential solved from disclosed cost of sales

crude_hist.source: Brent averages for the four historical periods, USD a barrel. HOUSE ESTIMATES read off the published price record for each window, not company disclosure. They matter less than they look: the crude level enters the margin on BOTH sides and very largely cancels, which the study demonstrates rather than asserts

fx_hist.source: USD/EGP averages for the four historical periods. The June-2024 figure is built month by month across the March-2024 float (eight months near 30.9, four near 47.5); the others are period averages of the published rate. HOUSE ESTIMATES

rf.source: Egypt 10-year local-currency government bond yield, 22.31% (house cost-of-capital reference, cached 21-Jul-2026 print, re-verified 06-Aug-2026)

sov_spread_cds.source: Egypt credit-default-swap-implied sovereign default spread, Damodaran January-2026 country-premium file, CDS column. Netted out of the local-currency risk-free rate so sovereign default risk is not charged twice

sov_spread_rating.source: Damodaran adjusted default spread on the rating basis, January-2026 — the alternative construction, disclosed for the audit trail

erp_cds.source: Damodaran original country-premium file, Egypt row, CDS column, last updated 5 January 2026 — total equity risk premium

erp_rating.source: Damodaran original country-premium file, Egypt row, rating basis, January-2026 — the alternative

policy_rate.source: Central Bank of Egypt main operation rate 19.50% (corridor 19.00/20.00), held at the third meeting of 2026 — a second consecutive hold

cpi.source: Egypt annual headline inflation 14.30% in June 2026, down from 14.60% in May. The central bank expects inflation to accelerate through the third quarter of 2026 on base effects, supply pressures and fiscal adjustment before resuming its decline

cbe_target.source: The central bank's own stated inflation target, 7% (+/-2pp) on average for the fourth quarter of 2026, falling to 5% (+/-2pp) for the fourth quarter of 2028

fx.source: USD/EGP 50.25; the pound closed at 50.30/50.40 on 4 August 2026. The 52-week range is 46.64-54.86, so the currency is not range-bound

fx_path.source: USD/EGP average-rate path, about 4.5% a year of depreciation from the 2025 average. Below the inflation differential, on the view that the post-float regime and the reserve build slow the pass-through — this is a genuine driver: both revenue legs are priced off dollar product benchmarks

fx_avg_cy25.source: USD/EGP average rate for calendar 2025, used to convert the dollar-denominated unit build back to the reported base year

tax_stat.source: Egypt corporate income tax 22.5%. AMOC is a downstream processor and is taxed at the ordinary corporate rate, not the ~40.55% rate that applies to exploration and production concessions

egypt_gdp_nominal.source: Egypt nominal gross domestic product, EGP mn, order of magnitude, used only for the terminal-growth crossover arithmetic

egypt_nominal_growth.source: Long-run Egyptian nominal growth used as the terminal ceiling for the domestic leg

world_nominal_growth.source: Long-run world nominal growth used as the terminal ceiling for the export leg

wacc_usd_rf.source: US 10-year Treasury yield used in the currency-of-discounting alternative

wacc_usd_erp.source: Blended emerging-market equity risk premium applied to the dollar-denominated alternative

beta.source: Own-stock tier-1 regression: AMOC weekly log-returns against a 33-name equal-weight Egyptian Exchange composite built from the full covered library, five-year window. R-squared 0.312, n = 257, standard error 0.087, 90% confidence interval [0.797, 1.084]. Passes the usability gate comfortably and is NOT a weak instrument: the interval spans 0.29x the point estimate, well inside the 2x flag

tax_eff.source: Effective tax rate used for NOPAT. Struck one percentage point above the 22.5% statutory rate for non-deductible items and the deferred-tax drag typical of Egyptian downstream filers

recv_days.source: Trade receivable days. The offtake is dominated by the state petroleum complex on short settlement, which is why a company turning over EGP 40bn of revenue runs a balance sheet of only EGP 8.1bn

inv_days.source: Inventory days on cost of sales. Feedstock is drawn from the adjacent refining complex rather than imported and stocked

pay_days.source: Trade payable days on cost of sales. The feedstock payable to the state petroleum corporation is the company's principal source of working-capital funding

other_ca.source: Other current assets, EGP mn, held flat

dna_pct.source: Depreciation and amortisation as a share of revenue. The complex was commissioned between 1997 and 2000 and is substantially written down, which is why the charge is small against turnover

capex_pct.source: Capital expenditure as a share of revenue, tapering. Anchored on the approved EGP 580.19mn budget against the same year's budgeted net sales of EGP 37.332bn, which is 1.55%; the taper reflects the completion of the current storage-tank and environmental programme

opex_pct.source: The net operating load between gross profit and EBITDA, as a share of revenue — selling, general and administrative costs and other expenses, less other operating income

cash_yield.source: Yield earned on the cash pile. Egyptian treasury bills and corporate deposits price a few points under the 19.50% policy rate net of the 20% withholding on interest

cash_yield_path.source: Forward path for the deposit yield, easing with the policy rate

kd.source: Marginal cost of debt. The gross book is EGP 25mn — 0.06% of revenue — of short-dated Egyptian-pound facilities, so the rate is taken at the corridor lending rate of 20.00% plus a 200bp corporate spread rather than pretended to be observable. The integrity gate below computes what this input is actually WORTH to the answer

kd_path.source: Forward cost-of-debt path 2026E-2030E, following the central bank's own disinflation path toward the long-run Egyptian corporate-borrowing norm. This path is what sets the SHAPE of the cost-of-capital glide; it is not a second free parameter

kd_term.source: Terminal cost of debt: the midpoint of the 14-16% long-run Egyptian corporate-borrowing norm, with no name-specific reason to deviate

real_rate_term.source: Terminal real risk-free rate, the standard emerging-market convention. The terminal NOMINAL risk-free rate is not an input: it is DERIVED as this real rate plus the central bank's inflation target IN FORCE for the terminal horizon (`cbe_target`), so the single most terminal-value-sensitive number in the model cannot be set by hand. The previous edition hardcoded 10.50% by adding 5.5pp to the 5% target dated Q4-2028 while describing it as 'the' medium-term target; the target in force is 7% for Q4-2026 and the July-2026 rate decision pushed even that to H2-2027

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised below the currently elevated crisis-era level toward the rating-class norm; never held flat into perpetuity

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight, normalised. The company is net cash today and has been for years; a terminal structure carrying a tenth of capital in debt is already generous to the valuation and avoids capitalising the current zero-leverage position into perpetuity

g_term.source: Terminal growth, 5% — the standing centre for established names in this market once currency turbulence has passed, sensitised 3-7%. An EGP-nominal rate struck against an EGP-nominal terminal risk-free rate

rel_rerating.source: Re-rating applied to the company's OWN trailing enterprise-value to EBITDA multiple in the relative lens. ZERO: the name is held at the multiple the market already pays it. The justified multiple is no longer a free number — it is DERIVED as the trailing multiple times one plus this figure, so it cannot drift away from the company's own pricing without the drift being visible. The previous edition set 4.5x by hand and justified it as 'holding the name at its own trailing level' against a stated trailing multiple of 'around 4.6x'; the model's own output was different, so the stated justification was false whichever way the multiple was struck. Holding at zero re-rating makes the lens a statement about the BRIDGE — what the disclosed claims on the cash are worth — rather than a disguised view on the multiple

pe_just.source: Justified through-cycle price-to-earnings multiple on normalised earnings. Trailing is about 7.5x on the constructed 2025 base. A single-asset processor with a 20% state shareholder, an administered feedstock relationship and an Egyptian cost of equity near 28% does not earn a premium multiple. Bear 5.5x / bull 9.5x

roe_sust.source: Sustainable return on equity for the book lens. Trailing return on average parent equity is about 33%; the sustainable rate is struck below it because the reported figure is flattered by a heavily written-down asset base that will have to be renewed

lens_weights.source: Discounted cash flow primary for a single-asset operating processor with a visible volume ramp; the relative and normalised-earnings lenses carry equal secondary weight; the book lens least, because a substantially depreciated plant makes book value a poor proxy for replacement cost

labels.vol_mult: Volume growth path, as a multiple of the assumed path
labels.gm_shift: Gross margin, shifted on every forecast year
labels.fx_mult: Exchange-rate path, as a multiple of the assumed path
labels.wacc_shift: Cost of capital, shifted at BOTH the explicit and terminal anchors

e1.method_short: earnings power at a justified multiple

e2.method_short: free cash flow to equity, discounted

e3.method_short: cash returns against the cost of capital

dq_log: dropped 1 rows carrying a non-positive or non-finite OHLC value (2013-05-07) — vendor fills, not tradeable prices

assert_log: AMOC — ASSERT / derivation log

[Base year — ALTERNATIVE: nine AUDITED months, annualised] the transition period 1-Jul-2025 to 31-Dec-2025 (audited, Crowe, unqualified) and the three months to 31-Mar-2026 (reviewed) are contiguous and cover nine months: net sales 31,247, cost of sales 28,901, GROSS PROFIT 2,345, a margin of 7.506%. Annualised at 4/3 that is 41,662 of revenue. This edition NO LONGER uses it as the headline base — see the twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 below — but publishes it as the alternative, because half of the twelve-month base is a press release rather than a filing.

[Base year — TWELVE CONTIGUOUS MONTHS to 30-Jun-2026, NO annualisation] the audited transition half (Jul-Dec 2025) plus the reported half (Jan-Jun 2026) is a clean twelve months: net sales 46,959, gross profit 4,225, margin 8.997%. NO 4/3 scalar is applied and no period is estimated. HALF OF THIS BASE IS NOT AUDITED and the study says so on every page that uses it. The released gross profit of 3,258 is REJECTED: run through the company's own Q1-2026 expense run rates it produces a profit after tax of 2,142 against a reported 1,903, +12.6% too high. The gross profit used, 2,951, is SOLVED from the release's own profit line, which passes two independent tests: majority profit ties to the AUDITED equity statement within 1.2%, and revenue ties to an independent triangulation within 0.2%. Implied Q2-2026 gross margin 11.96% against the 10.19% of Q1 — a rise, but not the 13.92% the released gross-profit line would require.

[Base year — SELECTED] twelve months to 30-Jun-2026. Revenue 46,959, gross margin 8.997%, against the nine-month annualisation's 41,662 and 7.506%. Both are published and the model runs on either; the twelve-month base is the headline because it needs no annualisation scalar, and the nine-month base is retained because all of it is audited or reviewed. The gap between the two is +12.7% on revenue and +1.49% on margin, and that gap is a real uncertainty about this company, not a rounding difference.

[Three rates, SOLVED not assumed] statutory tax 22.50% on operating profit (the effective 22.12% is struck on a pre-tax base that includes credit interest and a deferred credit, and is kept for the historical reconciliation only). Employees' profit share and board bonuses 5.27% of profit after tax, solved from the disclosed charge of 135 over profit of 2,559. Minority interest 3.258%, restruck over the whole base year and over OPERATING profit — against the 4.645% the previous edition called 'the DISCLOSED rate', which was a single-half ratio computed on a profit base that included the parent's own credit interest.

[Effective tax rate, computed not assumed] nine-month pre-tax profit 1,658 against a total tax charge of 367 (current less deferred, both periods) = 22.12%. The statutory rate is 22.5%. The previous edition assumed 22.1%.

[The margin record, as filed] 6M to Dec-2024 6.85% · 3M to Mar-2025 5.05% · 6M to Dec-2025 6.14% · 3M to Mar-2026 10.19%. This is not a modelled path and not a house assumption — it is gross profit over net sales in four consecutively filed periods. Note the shape: the margin was 6.85% in the half to December 2024, collapsed to 5.05% in the March-2025 quarter, recovered to 6.15% in the half to December 2025 and then printed 10.19% in the March-2026 quarter. The March-2026 print is the highest in the disclosed record by a wide margin and it is a SINGLE QUARTER; the base year above blends it with the half that precedes it rather than annualising it on its own.

[The cost stack, DISCLOSED not built] note 15-A splits the 19,462 of cost of sales in the transition half: raw materials 17,650 (90.7%), salaries 881 (4.5%), other — natural gas, electricity, water, spare parts, maintenance and the EPROM operating contract — 807 (4.1%), supporting materials 65 (0.3%) and depreciation 59 (0.3%). The previous edition BUILT a stack from house estimates of yields, energy intensity and a solved feedstock differential, carried NO salaries line at all inside cost of sales, and estimated chemicals at roughly five times the disclosed figure. None of that construction survives: the filing states the stack and the model uses it as stated.

[What this company actually is] raw materials are 85.1% of net sales. Every other cost line together is 5.9%. A business whose single largest line is 85% of revenue and whose gross margin is 9.0% is a PASS-THROUGH PROCESSOR: the value is not in the revenue line, and it is not in cost control either — it is in the spread between what the feedstock costs and what the slate fetches, and in the tonnage that spread is earned on.

[The product table, AUDITED] note 14-A gives eight lines with tonnes AND value for the transition half: 808,084 tonnes for 20,736. Realisations per tonne fall straight out of the division and nothing is reconstructed: Base and special oils 47,250 · Paraffin wax 48,881 · Gas oil 29,832 · Fuel oil (mix) 19,506 EGP a tonne. The specialty slate — oils and wax — is 11.97% of the tonnage and 22.37% of the value. The previous edition used a THREE-line table obtained from a reviewer rather than the filing, and had to reconstruct realisations through a crude-parity crack multiple. The filing makes all of that unnecessary: fuel oil (mix) alone is 56.9% of tonnage and 43.3% of value, and it is not the same product as gas oil, naphtha or LPG, which the old build had merged into one slate.

[Line-level value growth, half on half] Base and special oils +2.8% · Paraffin wax +21.3% · Gas oil -1.9% · Naphtha -7.3% · Liquefied petroleum gas +18.7% · Fuel oil (mix) +29.1% · Heavy fuel oil +60.7%. Wax is the standout at +21.3% and fuel oil at +29.1%; gas oil and naphtha both FELL. That is the mix shift the forecast has to carry, and it is measured rather than assumed.

[Cost, PER LINE — built, not blended] conversion runs Base and special oils 10,957 · Paraffin wax 12,601 · Gas oil 2,739 · Fuel oil (mix) 548 EGP a tonne on the registered processing-intensity weights; feedstock is then allocated on NET REALISABLE VALUE — realisation less that line's own conversion — which is the standard joint-product method and the only basis of the three tested that leaves every disclosed line with a positive spread. GROSS SPREAD PER TONNE: Base and special oils 4,182 · Paraffin wax 4,202 · Gas oil 3,051 · Naphtha 2,360 · Liquefied petroleum gas 3,666 · Fuel oil (mix) 2,117 · Heavy fuel oil 1,687 EGP. That is the number that matters and it is the one the previous edition could not produce: a tonne of base oil contributes 2.0 times the spread of a tonne of fuel oil, so the specialty mix is now a real driver of value. GROSS MARGIN BY LINE: Base and special oils 7.8% · Paraffin wax 7.6% · Gas oil 9.0% · Fuel oil (mix) 9.6% against a blended 9.0% — note that the specialty lines show a LOWER margin percentage on a HIGHER spread per tonne, because their realisation per tonne is nearly three times fuel oil's. Percentage margin is the wrong lens on a joint-product slate; spread per tonne is the right one, and the previous edition had neither.

[The one operating input that is not read off a filing] the processing-intensity weights Base and special oils 1.00 · Paraffin wax 1.15 · Gas oil 0.25 · Naphtha 0.20 · Liquefied petroleum gas 0.15 · Fuel oil (mix) 0.05 · Heavy fuel oil 0.05. Note 15-A discloses the cost stack for the company and NOT by line. Any weight derivable from note 14-A alone is a function of realisation, and a realisation-derived weight returns an identical margin on every line — which is the defect being removed. So this vector is a judgement, it is registered and dated like every other input, and section 7 treats it as a named weakness rather than burying it in a formula.

[Capital expenditure, BUILT] fixed assets at COST are 2,741 against an annual depreciation charge of 151, an implied asset life of 18.1 years. Maintenance capital expenditure is struck at cost over that life, 151 a year before inflation — against cash actually paid of 160. The company is spending 1.06 times replacement. GROWTH capital expenditure is charged at the plant's own capital intensity of 1,948 EGP of gross plant per annual tonne, so incremental tonnage now COSTS something instead of arriving free. The previous edition held one cash number flat and inflated it, which made volume growth self-funding.

[Working capital, BUILT on solved days] inventory 24.3 days of cost of sales, receivables 7.3 days of revenue, operating payables 13.1 days of cost of sales — every one SOLVED from the audited balance sheet against the base year, not assumed. The house registry carried 14/14/24 days and no formula read any of them. Dividends payable of 517 is REMOVED from creditors: a declared distribution to shareholders is a financing claim, and leaving it inside operating working capital both understated the capital the business ties up and let a shareholder claim vanish from the bridge. It is carried in the bridge instead.

[Balance sheet, AUDITED] property plant and equipment 893 plus projects under construction 407 = 1,300. Inventory 2,847, receivables and debtors 939, payables and creditors 2,052 -> NET WORKING CAPITAL 1,734. INVESTED CAPITAL 3,034. The previous edition reconstructed property plant and equipment as the residual against disclosed total assets and got 2,403 — 1.8 times the filed figure — and put net working capital at 2.0% of revenue against an actual 3.7%. Total assets matched only because the reconstruction was anchored on them; the composition was wrong in both directions.

[Net cash, AUDITED] cash 2,464 against long-term loans 11.8 and short-term loans 9.2: NET CASH 2,443 = EGP 1.89 a share, 20.8% of market capitalisation. A further 509 of deposits is PLEDGED against credit facilities and is deliberately NOT counted as free cash. Against it sits a tax-disputes provision of 921 — EGP 0.71 a share — which the previous edition never carried at all.

[Minority interest, DISCLOSED] the non-controlling share of group profit after tax is 4.645% in the audited half — AMOC owns 86.45% of Alexandria Wax Products. The previous edition INFERRED 3.0% from a gap between consolidated and standalone profit. It is now read off the filing.

[Cost of debt — MATERIALITY] gross debt is 0.1782% of the capital structure. A 500bp error in the cost of debt moves the weighted cost of capital by 0.69 basis points. The input cannot move the answer and the study says so rather than dressing an immaterial input as a precise one.

[Depreciation and capital expenditure, ACTUAL] over the twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 the company charged 151 of depreciation and right-of-use amortisation and paid 160 in cash for fixed assets and projects under construction. Cash capital expenditure is 1.06 times the depreciation charge and 1.06 times replacement at gross cost. The previous edition held the cash figure flat and inflated it, and separately stated that free cash flow was overstated by 'roughly EGP 2mn a year' — a claim that holds in the first forecast year and reverses sign in every year after it. Capital expenditure is now BUILT: maintenance at cost over the implied asset life, plus growth at the plant's own capital intensity, so the caveat is computed across the whole window instead of asserted for one year of it.

[Cost of equity] risk-free 22.31% less the sovereign default spread 3.40% = 18.91%; plus beta 0.941 times the equity risk premium 9.41% -> cost of equity 27.76%. Alternatives disclosed: on the rating basis 29.05%; the RETIRED un-netted construction 31.16%, kept only for the audit trail — it charges Egypt's sovereign default risk twice, once inside the pound yield and again in the country premium.

[Weighted cost of capital, explicit window] net debt is NEGATIVE, so the debt weight is -26.2% and the equity weight 126.2%. The cost of that negative debt is the blend of what the EGP 21mn borrowing costs and what the EGP 2,464mn cash pile EARNS: 13.21% after tax, i.e. essentially the after-tax deposit yield. Result 31.58% — ABOVE the 27.76% cost of equity, not below it. That direction is the point: a company holding 21% of its market capitalisation in near-riskless cash has an observed equity cost that UNDERSTATES the risk of its operating assets, so unlevering for the cash raises the operating rate. On a gross-debt basis the rate would be 27.74%; that construction discounts the operating cash flows at a rate the cash has already depressed AND then adds the cash back in the bridge, counting the cash twice and overstating the valuation. The net basis is primary and is the more conservative of the two by 384 basis points.

[Unlevering identity] enterprise value over market capitalisation (0.7922) times the operating rate, plus cash over market capitalisation (0.2078) times the cash cost, recombines to 27.7601% against a cost of equity of 27.7601% — exact. This is the check that the net-cash weighting is a decomposition rather than an adjustment.

[Weighted cost of capital, terminal] cost of equity 19.08% (norm-built risk-free 12.50% = the central bank's inflation target IN FORCE for the terminal emerging-market real-rate convention, plus beta times a normalised premium 7.00%); cost of debt after tax 11.68%; weights 90%/10% -> 18.34%. No terminal input is an observable quote and none is reverse-engineered from a price.

[Glide] forward cost of capital 31.58% -> 26.85% -> 23.07% -> 20.23% -> 18.34%; cumulative discount factors 0.7600, 0.5991, 0.4868, 0.4049, 0.3421. The glide fractions are the cost-of-debt path's own cumulative progress (0.000, 0.357, 0.643, 0.857, 1.000), so the front-loaded shape is inherited from the assumed easing calendar rather than being a second free parameter.

[Forecast revenue] 52,841 -> 58,432 -> 63,773 -> 68,952 -> 73,978 (volume 1.664 -> 1.817mn tonnes; specialty share of revenue 22.9% -> 24.1%). Base-year revenue is the twelve months to 30-Jun-2026, 46,959, with no annualisation scalar.

[Forecast gross margin] 8.61% -> 8.19% -> 7.77% -> 7.40% -> 7.00%. The margin is an OUTPUT of eight per-line cost builds, not a path and not a blend: each line carries its own feedstock cost per tonne and its own conversion cost per tonne, and the company margin is whatever the mix produces. Specialty lines run Base and special oils 6.9% · Paraffin wax 6.6% against fuel oil at 9.5%, so the margin now moves when the MIX moves, which it could not do when one blended margin was applied to every line.

[Capital expenditure, BUILT] 281 -> 307 -> 329 -> 351 -> 375 against depreciation 174 -> 189 -> 206 -> 224 -> 244. Ratio 1.62 · 1.62 · 1.59 · 1.56 · 1.54. Maintenance is 151 at today's prices, growth is charged at 1,948 EGP a tonne of new throughput, and depreciation ROLLS off the asset register rather than being held flat for five years.

[Employees' profit share, CHARGED] 5.27% of profit after tax, 97 -> 95 -> 90 -> 85 -> 76. The previous edition registered this at 67 for the audited half, described it in its own source note as 'a real distribution out of profit that the previous edition of this study did not model at all', and then no formula read the cell.
[Free cash flow to the firm] 826 -> 1,308 -> 1,231 -> 1,137 -> 978; present value of the explicit window 2,805.

[Forecast finance income] 414 -> 216 -> 130 -> 62 -> 5 — the charge is a CREDIT throughout and it falls even as the cash pile builds, because the deposit yield eases with the policy rate faster than the balance grows. Attributable profit 2,066, 1,882, 1,735, 1,585, 1,381; net cash 1,448, 972, 505, 46, -405 on a 103.7% payout.

[Return on invested capital] 44.0% / 39.2% / 34.2% / 29.7% / 24.8%; terminal return taken as next year's NOPAT over closing invested capital, 26.0%. The level is high because the plant is substantially written down and the working capital is negative-to-negligible — a real feature of the business, and the reason the required terminal reinvestment rate comes out low.

[Terminal growth, reconciled against the AUDITED record] gross margin as filed 6M Dec-2024 6.85% / 3M Mar-2025 5.05% / 6M Dec-2025 6.14% / 3M Mar-2026 10.19%. Annualised returns on invested capital 28.1% / 22.2% / 24.9% / 66.0%; reinvestment rates -6.9% / +12.7% / -10.5% / +4.9%; implied growth -1.9% / +2.8% / -2.6% / +3.2%.

[Terminal growth, the check that now BINDS] reinvestment is NEGATIVE in every audited period, because cash capital expenditure is running below the depreciation charge. Growth = return x reinvestment therefore implies a NEGATIVE steady-state growth rate of about 0.4%: on its own recent record this company is shrinking its capital base, not compounding it. The adopted terminal rate of 5.0% is NOT supported by the reinvestment identity and the study says so on its face rather than burying it. Two readings are defensible and both are published: either the under-investment is temporary and capital expenditure must rise toward depreciation — in which case free cash flow in the explicit window is overstated by roughly -107 a year — or it is durable and the terminal growth rate should be at or below zero. The sensitivity grid runs terminal growth down to 3% and the reader can go lower.

[Terminal growth, stated plainly] the two standing checks disagree with each other, and that is the honest reading rather than a problem to be smoothed. Check (a), the historical compound NOPAT rate, is +55.0% — far ABOVE the adopted 5.0%; it is a recovery rate off a devaluation-compressed base and belongs in the explicit years, not in perpetuity. Check (b), return times reinvestment from stable years, is 0.4% — BELOW the adopted rate. The adopted 5% sits between them and above the one that describes a steady state, so on the check that matters for a perpetuity it remains on the GENEROUS side of the company's own record. Sensitised 3-7%; the grid is on the face of the workbook. NOTE the reinvestment definition: check (b) uses net capex over NOPAT, EXCLUDING working capital, while the free-cash-flow waterfall subtracts working capital. On the waterfall-consistent definition the base-year reinvestment rate is 95.9% and the implied growth is 23.9% — ABOVE the adopted rate. Both definitions are shown; neither is hidden.

[Terminal value] the terminal return is struck on invested capital at REPLACEMENT cost — working capital plus the asset base at GROSS cost — giving 17.1%, against 26.0% on net book. The difference is not cosmetic: this plant is 67.4% written down, the book lens already haircuts return on equity from a reported 33% to 28% for exactly that reason, and using the flattered figure in the terminal block while haircutting it in the book lens would be two views of one asset base. Required reinvestment = growth / return = 5.0% / 17.1% = 29.3%; terminal value 7,573 capitalised at 18.34% and discounted at the YEAR-5 cumulative factor 0.3421, giving a present value of 2,591. TERMINAL VALUE IS 48.0% OF ENTERPRISE VALUE.

[Terminal reinvestment, against the explicit window] the final forecast year reinvests 28.21% of profit; the terminal block reinvests 29.32%. The step is +1.11% and it is disclosed here because it RAISES the terminal block, which carries 48.0% of enterprise value. It is a consequence of the steady-state identity rather than an assumption, but a reader is entitled to see it.

[Bridge — every disclosed claim carried] enterprise value 5,396 plus net cash 2,443 = 7,839. Less minority interests at 3.258% of the WHOLE enterprise including the cash (255) — the previous edition charged the minority its share of the operating enterprise and then credited the parent with 100% of the consolidated cash, which is an inconsistency a reader can find in one line. Less the tax-disputes provision 921, a recognised liability the previous edition quoted in its text and NEVER carried into the bridge — setting it to zero moved that valuation by nothing at all. Less dividends payable 517, a declared claim removed from working capital and carried here. Plus non-operating investments 578 — the equity stake at fair value through other comprehensive income and the PLEDGED deposits, which are real assets even though they are not free cash and were previously excluded from BOTH the cash line and the bridge. Equity attributable 6,723 = EGP 5.21 a share against a spot of EGP 9.10 (-42.8%).

[Contested choices, computed] (1) rating-basis cost of capital instead of the CDS basis: explicit 32.18% / terminal 22.15% -> EGP 5.43 (+4.3%). (2) minority share doubled to 6% -> EGP 6.09 (+17.0%). (3) GROSS-debt rather than net-debt weights, the construction this study rejects because it counts the cash pile twice -> EGP 6.41 (+23.1%).

[Currency-of-discounting alternative] the export leg (8% of cash flow) is first DEFLATED to dollars at each year's exchange rate, discounted at a dollar cost of capital of 10.72% with 3.5% terminal growth, and only then translated back at the spot rate. Discounting a pound-denominated cash flow already inflated by the assumed depreciation path directly at a dollar rate would count the currency benefit twice. Result EGP 6.21 a share (-31.8% against spot).

[Relative lens — on the TRAILING metric, multiple DERIVED] the company's own trailing multiple is 3.54x enterprise value to EBITDA — enterprise value 9,310 over base-year EBITDA 2,629 — and 7.1x earnings. The justified multiple is DERIVED from it at a +0% re-rating, 3.54x, rather than set by hand. The previous edition stated the trailing multiple as 'around 4.6x' and then set 4.5x, calling that 'holding the name at its own trailing level'; the model's own output disagreed with the stated 4.6x, so the justification did not hold whichever multiple was right. 3.54x on TRAILING EBITDA gives an enterprise value of 9,310 TODAY, carried through the SAME bridge as the cash-flow lens -> EGP 8.14 a share. Nothing here is discounted at the cash-flow lens's rate and nothing is added back from it, so the difference between this lens and the spot price is entirely the BRIDGE: the tax-disputes provision, the declared dividend and the minority's share of the cash. That is what this lens is now for.

[Normalised earnings lens — separated and discounted] OPERATING earnings only: 2028E operating profit 2,205, taxed at the statutory 22.5%, less the employees' profit share and the minority -> EGP 1.213 a share. At 7.5x that is EGP 9.10 AS AT mid-2028, discounted 2.4 years to the valuation date at the COST OF EQUITY 27.76% (factor 0.5555) = EGP 5.05. Net cash less the provision and the declared dividend is then added at FACE, outside the multiple: EGP 0.78 a share. Total EGP 5.83. The previous edition capitalised 301 of credit interest at an operating multiple — valuing a bank deposit as though it were the refinery — and then did not discount the 2028 answer at all, while lens 2 in the same document discounted its forward number. One lens discounted and the other did not; both are now on the valuation date.

[Book lens — on a rate path consistent with lens 1] justified price-to-book 1.23x = (sustainable return 28.0% less growth 5%) / (cost of equity 23.66% less growth), applied to book value of EGP 3.71 a share -> EGP 4.57. The rate is the present-value-weighted average of the SAME cost-of-equity glide the cash-flow lens uses, 27.76% falling to 19.08%, not the terminal rate alone. Using the terminal rate alone gives 6.06 and using the explicit rate alone gives 3.75; a perpetuity beginning today deserves neither endpoint. Trailing return on average parent equity is 32.6%, and the sustainable rate is struck below it because the asset base is 67.4% written down — the same haircut now applied to the terminal return in lens 1, so there is one view of the asset base across the model rather than two.

[Scenarios on the cash-flow lens] bear EGP 2.76 / base EGP 5.21 / bull EGP 9.34. The scenarios are FIVE simultaneous driver moves, not a single lever: volume growth at 0.4x / 1.5x the assumed path, gross margin -1.0% / +1.0%, the exchange-rate path -3% / +3%, the cost of capital +2% / -2% at both anchors, and terminal growth 3% / 6%. Because all five move together and in the same direction, the bear and bull ends are JOINT-worst and JOINT-best cases and are much wider than any single-driver row in the sensitivity table; they are not a confidence interval and no probability is attached to them.
